proven: Only one of two independent SQL claim connections wins a queued job.
Missing/old tokens cannot start, heartbeat or overwrite a new attempt; the current claimant can finish once.
Cancellation revokes the attempt; a manual retry gets a new job identity.
Heartbeat preserves liveness, stale recovery revokes ownership and exhausted attempts cannot claim again.
Push/named/pull claims refuse to run before the existing token/heartbeat migration.
Hung/refused renewal aborts local execution; fenced work cannot invoke a new task or publish a refused terminal result.
Long maintenance holds renew; displacement aborts callbacks and does not delete the replacement lock.
rollout: Apply schema/local_compute_worker_schema.sql before deploying the new push executor.
Drain/stop old push executors before enabling new claims; their unconditional SQL is not safe during mixed-version execution.
Current push and pull claims survive boot until the normal stale window; immediate boot cleanup is only for legacy tokenless rows.
limits: Local PostgreSQL exercises production statements but does not prove Aurora Data API or AWS deployment.
Abort is cooperative; already-issued remote business effects still need durable idempotency.
Attempt fencing is per job; fleet-wide box admission/capacity is not newly accepted.
No cloud deployment, shared mock reset, Redis Cluster or production throughput acceptance.
